beats.beat: Specialty chemicals are not commodities; they are chemicals sold for a specific function. The company's four product groups are Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals.
The company claims a diversified product portfolio and diversified user industries as competitive strengths, along with import substitution potential.
Its sales route is the single most important fact about the business: a long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited to market and sell products through the promoter's network.

Sales are not committed by long-term contracts. The filing says the company relies on purchase orders from customers for volume, pricing and other terms, and it has no long-term agreements with raw material suppliers either.
Customer concentration is high: top ten customers were roughly 59% of revenue from operations in FY17, 57% in FY16 and 59% in FY15.
There is an export book, albeit small: about Rs 1,068.18 lakh of exports in aggregate over the past five years, to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.
The company also lists product innovation/R&D and strong management as strengths, and leans on the support of its holding company.

beats.beat: The restated financials cover six periods: the six months ended September 30, 2017, and the fiscals ended March 31, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014 and 2013.

Profit after tax: the company was in loss in FY13 (Rs -27.40 lakh) and FY14 (Rs -12.17 lakh), then turned profitable — Rs 149.58 lakh in FY15, Rs 90.18 lakh in FY16, Rs 174.82 lakh in FY17 and Rs 132.75 lakh in H1 FY18.
Basic EPS follows the same shape: Rs -0.45 in FY13, Rs -0.20 in FY14, then Rs 2.47, Rs 1.46, Rs 2.43 and Rs 1.48 in FY15, FY16, FY17 and H1 FY18.

Operating cash flow tells a more nervous story: Rs 200.97 lakh in FY13, Rs 127.73 lakh in FY14, Rs 422.36 lakh in FY15, Rs 802.59 lakh in FY16, then a negative Rs 349.75 lakh in FY17, recovering to Rs 124.86 lakh in H1 FY18.
Total assets: Rs 3,018.66 lakh in FY13, Rs 2,679.38 lakh in FY14, Rs 2,592.53 lakh in FY15, Rs 2,767.21 lakh in FY16, Rs 3,273.96 lakh in FY17, Rs 3,424.96 lakh at Sep 30, 2017.

beats.beat: Promoters: Mr Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr Atil C. Parikh and Mr Rajesh C. Parikh, along with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited.
They hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of pre-issue paid-up capital; promoter group members other than promoters hold 21,510 shares, or 0.24%.
Capital base: authorised capital is Rs 2,000 lakh and issued, subscribed and paid-up capital is Rs 897 lakh — 89,70,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each.
The company has had related-party transactions in each of the last five financial years and the six months ended Sep 30, 2017, disclosed under Accounting Standard 18.
It also discloses that it, its promoters, group company and directors face certain legal proceedings, and that an unfavourable outcome could have a material effect.
Past RoC filings have not been flawless: the DRHP acknowledges instances of non-filing, incorrect filing or delay, sometimes corrected by paying additional fees.

beats.beat: The relevant market is India's specialty chemicals industry, estimated at roughly Rs 1,000 billion in FY17 — about 17% of a chemicals industry the filing puts at Rs 5,800-6,200 billion.
Growth: specialty chemicals grew at 10-12% CAGR from FY14 to FY17, and CRISIL Research is quoted forecasting 12-14% CAGR ahead.

Fastest-moving uses: construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients are each expected to grow at 15% CAGR; surfactants at 13%; textile chemicals and flavours-and-fragrances at 12%; polymer additives at 10%.

Demand drivers the filing cites: rising consumption intensity, a middle-class that could reach 148 million households by 2030, a Draft National Chemical Policy, FDI up to 100% in the sector, and China's tighter environmental rules shifting the global balance.
Competition is fragmented but real: SMEs hold 70-75% of the market, and only a few Indian players have the scale to take on global giants in innovation.
The import-substitution argument has a statistical base: chemicals imports grew at 6.4% CAGR in the five years to FY17, slightly faster than exports at 6%.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes minerals into specialty chemicals — Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals — and sells them to industrial users. What makes the model unusual: it markets and sells through the network of its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.
The issue is aimed at the SME segment of the stock market: the company proposes to list on NSE Emerge, the SME platform of NSE, to create a public trading market for its shares.
Fresh capital will go mainly towards a new manufacturing facility at GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and general corporate purposes.
Control sits with the Parikh family and the corporate promoter: together they hold 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.

beats.beat: The issue is managed by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited as lead manager; Link Intime India Private Limited is the registrar.

Stated objects: fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; general corporate purposes; and create a public trading market by listing on NSE Emerge.
The pages reviewed do not show an issue size, price band, or whether any shares are being sold by existing shareholders — those figures are not in the extracts used for this report.

offer.heading: The offer: a fresh-issue funded new plant, listed on NSE Emerge
offer.purpose: Name the managers and the stated use of proceeds, and flag what the extracts do not disclose.

beats.beat: Revenue concentration without contracts: top-10 customers generate about 59% of revenue, and sales are governed by purchase orders — there are no long-term customer agreements, so volume and price can move quickly.
The distributor is the parent: products reach customers through the corporate promoter's network under a long-term arrangement; a breakdown in that relationship would hit the route to market.
Compliance gaps: the company has not yet obtained all statutory and regulatory approvals needed to operate its facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Gujarat, and has had past RoC filing lapses.
Cash flow can turn negative: FY17 operating cash flow was a minus Rs 349.75 lakh despite a profit, and the company's risk section concedes earlier years also saw negative cash flows.

Much of the property is rented: the company does not own its manufacturing facilities at Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Tirunelveli, nor its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur.
